edges.description: Cyp51-mediated lanosterol demethylation permits the remaining fungal sterol reactions that yield ergosterol.
Ergosterol produced by the causal fungi is incorporated into their plasma membranes, where it supports membrane organization.
intermediate_mechanisms: ergosterol insertion into the fungal plasma membrane
sterol-dependent membrane packing and membrane-protein organization

nodes.description: Completion of sterol biosynthesis produces ergosterol for the plasma membranes of the dematiaceous fungi that cause chromoblastomycosis. This is the normal molecular output downstream of the azole target.

evidence.reference_title: Terbinafine: mode of action and properties of the squalene epoxidase inhibition.
evidence.snippet: Treated fungi accumulate squalene while becoming deficient in ergosterol, an essential component of fungal cell membranes.

nodes.description: Ergosterol incorporation supports organization and integrity of the plasma membranes of chromoblastomycosis-causing fungi. This node records the normal cellular output of ergosterol biosynthesis rather than drug-induced depletion or fungal killing.

evidence.reference_title: Terbinafine: mode of action and properties of the squalene epoxidase inhibition.
evidence.snippet: Treated fungi accumulate squalene while becoming deficient in ergosterol, an essential component of fungal cell membranes.

nodes.description: The dematiaceous fungi that cause chromoblastomycosis depend on fungal sterol 14-alpha-demethylase in the ergosterol pathway. This normal Cyp51/Erg11 enzyme activity is the disease-local therapeutic vulnerability inhibited by the itraconazole component of combination antifungal therapy.

evidence.reference_title: Sterol 14α-Demethylase Ligand-Binding Pocket-Mediated Acquired and Intrinsic Azole Resistance in Fungal Pathogens.
evidence.snippet: The fungal cytochrome P450 enzyme sterol 14α-demethylase (SDM) is a key enzyme in the ergosterol biosynthesis pathway.

nodes.description: Itraconazole was used together with terbinafine for three months in the cited chromoblastomycosis case. This treatment record models only the itraconazole component and does not assert itraconazole monotherapy or first-line status. The separate terbinafine/Erg1 branch is not modeled in this minimal Cyp51 conformer.

evidence.snippet: The patient has been treated with a combination of terbinafine and itraconazole for 3 months with a good clinical response.
